human_notes._source: one 30-second roundup segment (G7_rhN9V-pU) + jar research in chains_research/eldritch_end.json. Everything tagged [jar] is from the jar work, not video.
entry: None stated by any video. [jar] The real entry is geographic: the mod adds no dimension and no starter machine - you enter it by finding its two End biomes, the Primordial Abyss and the Hasturian Wastes, after the dragon. First quests should be 'stand in the biome / collect its surface blocks' (spire_stone, abysmal_fronds, hasturian_moss), then Etyr ore.

The roundup's one mechanical claim matches the jar's corruption system: the aberrations do not wait to be hunted, they come to stalk YOU - corruption accrues to the player and draws the mod's horrors out. Quest text should frame the mod as something that happens to the player, not a checklist they walk up to.
gates: [jar] Corruption gates the mid-game: Ominous Eyes only haunt players who have accumulated corruption, and their 15% drop rings the Eldritch Pedestal. You cannot speedrun the summoning altar without engaging the corruption mechanic.

[jar] The Faceless (the boss) is summon-only, via the pedestal ritual (Abysmal Pedestal from eight Aberration's Limbs, bound with chains and four Ominous Eyes, consuming an Aberration's Heart) - it is never found wild.
[jar] The armour tier (etyrite, beyond netherite) is gated on a netherite base plus the runtime-loot-injected etyr_upgrade_pattern.
traps: NOT VERIFIED BY VIDEO - no narrated guide exists to warn about anything. The jar-side traps from chains_research remain the authority: eldritch_end:hastur is unregistered (a kill:hastur task can never complete), eye/crystal exist only under Spell Engine compat, and the chorb spawn egg has no entity. The 6-second official teaser titles Hastur 'the King in Yellow' - he is marketing, not obtainable content in 0.3.4.

The mod's showcase videos are pure atmosphere; a player following YouTube will know the boss's look but not the summoning recipe. Quest descriptions must carry the ritual steps themselves rather than assume outside knowledge.
taught: The only thing video evidence teaches: the mod's identity and draw. It is pitched as the Lovecraftian nightmare option among End overhauls - the segment's whole thesis is that corruption of everything is the destination - with aberrations stalking the player and bosses standing between them and eldritch powers. Horror-toned quest chapter framing is faithful to how the mod is sold.
